title: Where Swift runs besides the iPhone: macOS, server and Linux

videos.script: Nineteen lessons ran on Linux, and every program in them would run on an iPhone too. This lesson asks where else Swift runs, and what changes when it does. {{platforms}} First the list. The release you installed was published for Linux, for Windows, and as bundles for other targets. Apple's own systems get their Swift inside Xcode. {{foundation}} Then the layer that differs. The language is the same everywhere. Foundation is not. You will see code ask, while compiling, which system it is on, and one import that a Mac never needs. {{server}} Then Swift where most of it runs off the phone: a server. The planner's week, answered over HTTP, and a client in the same language reading it back. {{static}} Then a program that carries its own runtime. Built once, copied to a machine that has never seen Swift, and run there. {{mac}} Then what a Mac adds, described and not run. {{next}} And last, what the next course takes from this one, lesson by lesson. By the end you know where the wall is, and which side of it you are on.
